screening_reasoning: Presents the vision and early prototype of the TIB AIssistant, a domain-agnostic platform with modular orchestration for research-lifecycle tasks including literature analysis. No formal quantitative evaluation yet, hence moderate confidence.

meta-pipe is an open-source 10-stage LLM-agent pipeline covering the full SR/MA workflow with five mandatory human gates, GRADE assessment, and overclaim detection across 12 hallucination patterns. System description with quantitative cost analysis and architectural comparison against five existing tools.

QBD-RankedDataGen generates custom ranked datasets for query-by-document retrieval in IR engineering (TREC benchmarks, BM25 tuning). The work addresses information retrieval dataset creation, not a scholarly literature review workflow or harness.

Empirical study of citation hallucination across four LLMs under deployment-motivated prompting constraints, using a deterministic Crossref+Semantic Scholar verification pipeline over 17,443 citations. Directly addresses citation integrity (INC-03) with quantitative evaluation; does not propose a literature workflow tool (no INC-01).

Narrative review of discriminative and generative AI applications in rheumatology (diagnosis, prognosis, drug discovery). Domain-specific clinical review with no computational system, architecture, or empirical artifact for literature workflows.

Evaluates LLM probability-score outputs for title/abstract screening in SLR automation, comparing four models on consistency between qualitative and continuous ratings. Provides quantitative performance metrics directly relevant to SLR screening tool evaluation.

Evaluates the use of LLMs for SLR automation focusing on quality and time savings. No abstract available; inclusion is based on title and venue signaling an empirical evaluation of LLM-based SLR automation, hence lower confidence.

Proposes an LLM-based screening prioritization method for SLR automation achieving ~70% work-effort savings at 95% recall across four zoonotic-disease datasets. Includes explainable-AI rationales and validates recall metrics, directly relevant to literature review tool evaluation.
Framework and review of LLM applications in the healthcare/medical domain covering clinical tasks and research workflows. Healthcare domain focus, not an academic literature research harness or tool.

Commentary discussing LLM data extraction findings from a living review of clinical evidence synthesis and their implications for toxicology. No computational system or artifact; primarily opinion and discussion of existing work.

LLAssist is an open-source tool leveraging LLMs and NLP to automate literature review by extracting key information and evaluating relevance to user-defined research questions. Directly targets literature review automation with an accessible codebase.

Case study evaluating GPT-4o Mini and Claude 3.5 Sonnet for title/abstract screening in a precision-livestock-farming SLR, comparing accuracy, time, and cost against two human raters. Provides empirical evaluation of LLM-assisted screening tools.

Clinical study evaluating eight LLMs for reliability of parental health information on early maxillary expansion in dentistry. Medical/clinical domain; no scholarly literature workflow or research harness.

OpenScholar (Nature publication) is a retrieval-augmented LM over 45M open-access papers that achieves citation accuracy on par with experts while GPT-4o hallucinates 78–90% of citations. Fully open-source with code, models, datastore, and a new multi-domain ScholarQABench benchmark.

Living systematic review tracking 117 publications on (semi)automated data-extraction methods for SRs, including LLMs. Provides a broad evidence base with code/data availability analysis and documents emerging LLM-based extraction trends and reporting-quality concerns.

Presents and compares NLP approaches (spaCy, Simple T5, GPT-3.5-turbo RAG) for automated literature review generation from PDFs, evaluated via ROUGE scores on SciTLDR. Includes a GUI prototype for the best-performing system.

Proposes a transformer-based QA model for citation-context extraction from academic papers. No abstract available; inclusion is based on title and venue indicating a computational tool for scholarly citation analysis, but no quantitative evaluation is confirmed.

Introduces a multi-AI-agent system that automates the full SLR workflow—search string generation, screening, summarization, and research-question analysis—with empirical evaluation and open-source code on GitHub.

OpenScholar (arXiv original) is a retrieval-augmented LM querying 45M papers with citation accuracy on par with experts versus 78–90% hallucination in GPT-4o. Evaluated on ScholarQABench with fully open-source code, models, and datastore.

Review of machine learning methods for analyzing construction-industry accident reports, focusing on NLP text preprocessing and data mining. Construction safety domain, not an academic literature research harness.
